newsitem.title: UK: Baltic Index tops 1,500 for first time since Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Index tops 1,500 for first time since Jan 31.

text.p: Dry cargo freight rates extended a dramatic rally on Monday with a gain of 25 points on the Baltic Freight Index taking it above 1,500 for the first time since January 31.
The daily index of rates on key dry cargo routes, compiled by London's Baltic Exchange, reached 1,502.
It had registered a huge fall from a historic peak of 2,352 in May 1995 to a low at 992 this September before the current rebound.

Shipbrokers blamed that decline on a glut of new ships entering the market for bulk dry cargo -- grains, coal and ores. The recovery reflects unexpectedly strong demand for ships to take grain, coal, ores and fertiliser to Asia.
Signficantly higher rates for vessels in the Panamax category were again reported on Monday from the US Gulf.

Cobelfret have fixed Diavolezza 59,000 tonnes heavy grains Mississippi/Hamburg for 1-10 December at $14.10 per long ton and Andre have fixed Giovanni Bottiglieri for 55,000 tonnes soybeans US Gulf/China for mid-November at $28.

Brokers said the most spectacular fixture of the day was that of Stalo 73,000 dwt delivery South West Pass 16-25 November trip Singapore/Japan range at $16,000 daily plus a $300,000 ballast bonus to Glencore.

In the Pacific brokers reported a steady but quiet start to the week and the market generally for the bigger Capesize category of ship is looking promising but has yet to show the dramatic improvement seen in the Panamaxes.
Rates for the smaller Handy-sizes continue disappoint owners except from the European Continent.
